rationale: I read the complete held EO 13762 (82 FR 7619, Jan. 19, 2017, signed Jan. 13, 2017): an order of succession within the Department of Justice (acting Attorney General: the U.S. Attorneys for D.C., N.D. Ill. and C.D. Cal.), with sec. 3 revoking EO 13557; no own term. I read the held full text of EO 13775 (82 FR 10697, Feb. 14, 2017, signed Feb. 9, 2017): it sets a new order of succession and sec. 3 'Revocation of Executive Order. Executive Order 13762 of January 13, 2017, is revoked.' That names EO 13762 by number and number-and-date, covers the whole order, has no exception or savings clause, and EO 13762 has no part that survives. D6 self-check: the later events are EO 13775 itself and EO 13787 (82 FR 16723, Apr. 5, 2017, signed Mar. 31, 2017), whose sec. 3 revokes EO 13775 and sets a new succession list; I read EO 13787 in full and it contains no wording reviving, restoring or re-adopting EO 13762 or EO 13557, so the revocation of the revoking order does not bring EO 13762 back. The other held texts that contain the number 13762 (EO 11501-11503, 12993) are hash or page-number noise. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 13775, February 9, 2017' agrees but is a lead only. Provisional NO hypothesis; effective date of the revocation (on signing, Feb. 9, 2017) is not otherwise adjudicated.
